meta.title: Carrie the Swiss · Read the papers before you buy the puppy
meta.description: An animated series hosted by Carrie, a real Greater Swiss Mountain Dog from Slovakia. Pedigrees, health tests, dog shows and responsible breeding, explained with checked facts.

hero.ch1_text: A Greater Swiss Mountain Dog and a show dog. I'll teach you to choose a puppy by its papers, not its photo.
hero.ch2_title: Every puppy looks perfect in a photo.
hero.ch2_text: The papers tell the truth: pedigree, X-rays, show critiques and breed evaluation. I'll show you how to read them, one short episode at a time.
hero.ch3_title: My humans knew none of this. They learned it with me.
hero.ch3_text: Hips A/A, elbows 0/0, breed evaluation 14 out of 14. Facts by the FCI rules, no drama, a few jokes. You'll learn it faster: in twelve short episodes.

guide.eyebrow: What didn't fit in the video
guide.title: What my papers actually mean.
guide.intro: The longer version of each topic, with sources. Rules differ by country and breed club, so always ask yours.
guide.a1_lead: HD-A, ED-0, OCD-free. What the letters next to a puppy's parents mean.
guide.a1_p1: These joint problems are partly inherited, which is why good breeders X-ray both parents. Great scores lower the risk; they don't erase it. Fast growth and extra weight still count.
guide.a1_p2: A to E is the FCI scale used in Europe. In the US the OFA grades hips from Excellent to Severe, and in the UK the BVA/KC scheme gives a hip score. Ask which scale the papers use.
guide.a2_title: A pedigree is not the whole story
guide.a2_lead: It proves who a puppy comes from, not how it was raised.
guide.a2_p1: The FCI says it itself: a pedigree certifies parentage, not quality. A sunny living room with a mom you can meet, or a garage where the mom is "not available": both puppies can get the same paper.
guide.a2_p2: Check instead: both parents' health results on paper, the mom at the breeder's home with her puppies, and a breeder who asks you questions.
guide.a2_p3: The FCI doesn't issue pedigrees. Your national kennel club does. In Slovakia that's the SKJ, from the Slovak studbook (SPKP).
guide.a3_lead: Once in a dog's life, a committee decides if it may have puppies.
guide.a3_p1: To get in (Slovakia): X-rays of hips (A to C), elbows (0 to 1) and shoulders (clear), a CAC from two dog shows, and at least 15 months of age (18 for males).
guide.a3_p2: Character: seven tasks worth 2, 1 or 0 points each, from walking on the lead and a stranger taking the leash to wobbly ground, loud music and a distant bang. 11 points or more is excellent.
guide.a3_p3: Body: measurements against the standard (females 60 to 68 cm at the withers), bite and teeth, eye colour, build and temperament. When a breeder says a dog passed, ask to see the card.
guide.a4_title: How a responsible litter is planned
guide.a4_lead: Step one isn't finding a boyfriend.
guide.a4_p1: The mom is old enough, healthy and approved for breeding. The dad is not the closest one but the best match: healthy, good-natured and strong where she is weaker.
guide.a4_p2: Breeders check how related the pair is (the inbreeding coefficient, COI). The FCI recommends that no dog should have more offspring than 5% of the puppies registered in the breed over five years.
guide.a4_p3: Progesterone tests find the fertile days, and pregnancy takes about 63 days. Good breeders often have families waiting, and take a dog back at any age.

quiz.title: Is a Swissy right for you?
quiz.intro: Five honest questions. My humans answered them before they chose a breed. It worked.
quiz.q1: How much space do you have?
quiz.q1b: A house with a small garden
quiz.q1c: Lots of space and fields nearby
quiz.q2: How much time can you spend outside with me every day?
quiz.q2c: Two hours or more, rain or shine
quiz.q3: How do you feel about dog hair?
quiz.q4: An adult Swissy can weigh 40 to 60 kg. Can you handle that?
quiz.q5: We grow up slowly and stay puppies at heart for about three years. Patience?
quiz.r1_title: Maybe not a Swissy. And that's okay.
quiz.r1_text: Honest answer: a smaller or calmer breed might make you both happier. Choosing the right dog is a good decision too.
quiz.r2_title: It could work, with a plan.
quiz.r2_text: Meet adult Swissies, talk to a few breeders and plan the training before the puppy comes home.
quiz.r3_title: You might be my kind of human.
quiz.r3_text: Next step: find a breeder who shows you all the papers. Season one tells you what to look for.

ask.title: Ask the dog.
ask.intro: Breeding, puppies, health, training, feeding, shows. I've got time for all of it.
ask.note: My answers are AI-generated from what I've learned for the series. For your own dog's health, always ask your vet.
ask.hello: Hi! I'm Carrie. What would you like to know?
ask.c1: How do I spot a good breeder?
ask.c2: What do HD-A and ED-0 mean?
ask.c3: Is a Swissy good for a flat?
ask.c4: How should I feed a big puppy?
ask.err_rate: Woof, that's a lot of questions! Give me a minute to catch my breath.
ask.err_gen: Hmm, I lost my train of thought. Try again in a moment?
ask.err_off: I'm still learning to talk here. Back very soon!
ask.story:
My humans had never heard of my breed. They wanted a dog for the family, so they sat down and wrote honestly how they live, how much time they have and what they expect from a dog. That's how they arrived at a Swissy. And they wanted a dog with papers, because they didn't want to support anyone who sells puppies without them.

Then I arrived, and it began: training from day one, a first show "just to see how it works", the club, new friends, a second and a third show, X-rays, tests. And one confession: my human knew almost none of what I explain today. He learned it all with me.

These videos are the ones he wishes he'd had before he ever got a puppy. That's why they're free. May they help as many people as possible. And as many dogs.

album.title: From a tiny puppy to fourteen out of fourteen.
album.intro: My real photos and my real papers. I blacked out the private bits, the rest is exactly what the judges wrote.
album.c1_x: I was born in Slovakia on 28 March 2025, a tricolour Swissy girl with very big paws. Like every puppy from a registered litter, I got a pedigree from the Slovak studbook.
album.c2_t: My first dog show. I was six months old.
album.c2_x: Minor puppy class, "very promising", first place. The judge liked my head, ears and my excellent temperament… and wrote that I "need more training". Fair.
album.c3_t: Growing up, one paw at a time.
album.c3_x: Swissies grow slowly: paws first, legs next, the rest of me eventually. My humans call this my "teenage phase".
album.c4_x: Ten months old and very serious about it. Red harness, frozen field, zero regrets.
album.c5_t: Club show at 14 months: Excellent, first place.
album.c5_x: Even an "excellent" comes with homework. The judge noted a narrower head, steeper hind angulation and looser elbows on the move, and also my friendly nature. That's what a good critique looks like: honest.
album.c6_x: Excellent, first place, and a CAJC, the junior champion certificate. One more step towards my breed evaluation.
album.c7_x: Day one: Excellent 1, CAJC, CACIB Junior, Best Junior of Breed and Best of Breed. Days two and three: Excellent 1 again. Same dog, three opinions: "nice head expression", "could be fuller under the eyes", "slightly longer format". Judges are people too.
album.c8_x: Hips A/A, elbows 0/0, shoulders clear, knees and eyes clear. Ribbons are nice. X-rays are what keep my future puppies healthy.
album.c9_x: My breed evaluation: seven character tasks, full points, a body that matches the standard. Verdict: approved for breeding. I will be mentioning this.
album.c10_t: And today, I host a series.
album.c10_x: Nineteen months old, still a puppy at heart, and now I explain the papers to you. Thanks for reading my album.

house.wall_say: Real photos, real critiques. I blacked out the private details; the rest is in the judges' own words.
house.w1_x: I was born on 28 March 2025. Here I had just arrived home: big paws, bigger ears and zero idea what was off limits. I found that out later. On my own.
house.w2_t: My first show. I was six months old.
house.w2_x: Veľký Meder, my breed club's special show. The judge gave me "very promising 1" and wrote that I need more training. He was right. But that 1 is mine.
house.w3_x: First my paws grew, then my legs, and the rest is still deciding. Swissies grow up slowly, almost three years. My humans call it patience. I call it growth.
house.w4_x: I learned that snow can be eaten, dug and carried home on your nose. Red harness, frozen field, zero regrets.
house.w5_x: Club show at 14 months: excellent 1. But the judge also wrote down what isn't perfect yet. That's exactly the kind of critique you want to see when you pick a puppy: honest.
house.w6_x: An international show, excellent 1 and a junior championship certificate. The judge gave it to me; I left him some hair on his trousers in return.
house.w7_x: Rumanová: excellent 1 three times, and on day one Best of Breed, the best of all Swissies at the show. Same dog, three critiques. That's why you never trust a single paper.
house.w8_x: Hips A/A, elbows 0/0, shoulders clear. For a big breed that matters more than any trophy. Healthy joints mean more years of running.
house.w9_x: My breed evaluation: seven character tasks and a body check against the standard. Strangers, another dog, loud music and a bang in the distance. Full marks, verdict: approved for breeding.
house.w10_t: And today I host a show.
house.w10_x: I explain what's in the papers, how to read a critique and why a good puppy isn't cheap. Only I am animated. Everything else is real.
